crimlab: Statistical Toolkit for Criminology and Sociolegal Research

Source: R/crimlab.R
crimlab-package.Rd

Statistical methods for courts, corrections, policing, forensics and sociolegal research, computed in a compiled 'C++' core. Disparity tests: the veil-of-darkness contrast of Grogger and Ridgeway (2006) doi:10.1198/016214506000000168 , the outcome test and its infra-marginality problem, benchmark decomposition of resident disparities, dyadic offending rates, and the bounds a relative risk obeys given an odds ratio. Forensic methods: genotype match probabilities with the correction of Balding and Nichols (1994) doi:10.1016/0379-0738(94)90222-4 , the log-likelihood-ratio cost of Brummer and du Preez (2006) doi:10.1016/j.csl.2005.08.001 with its calibrated minimum, mixture likelihood ratios, kinship and paternity indices, database-search corrections, and Tippett and empirical-cross-entropy plots. Policy evaluation: difference in differences, event studies, staggered adoption, synthetic control and regression discontinuity, with their plots. Also measures of sentencing and custody, co-offending networks, spatial statistics of incidents, year-over-year change, survey estimates and audits of risk scores. Where an identity or bound has a machine-checked proof ('Lean'), the package names the theorem.

Notice of a newer release

The package makes no request on its own. updchk() asks the release page once, when called. A notice at attach is off unless turned on: with options(crimlab.update = TRUE) before the package is attached (in .Rprofile, say), or the environment variable CRIMLAB_UPDATE_CHECK set to 1, an interactive session then says in one line when a newer release exists. The page of the latest release is asked for at most once a day, with a limit of two seconds, and the answer is kept in tools::R_user_dir("crimlab", "cache"); nothing is sent but that request, and a failure is silent. A session that is not interactive (a script, a check, a test) never asks. options(crimlab.update = FALSE), or unsetting the variable, turns the notice off again.
